text:
Alex P: Heads-up — prepping Redwood Private install in customer VPC next week. Need a final plan for AWS KMS BYOK + envelope encryption for both control-plane and data-plane. Quick list: who hosts the CMK (customer vs redwood), cross-account key policy, DEK caching TTL, rotation & rewrap procedure, CloudTrail audit knobs. @Maya R @Chris L please weigh in.

Maya R: For regulated installs I strongly prefer customer-managed CMKs (BYOK) in the customer account. We should support: (1) customer CMK with cross-account access (preferred), (2) Redwood-managed CMK as fallback. For cross-account, key policy should explicitly allow the Redwood control-plane IAM role and the dedicated decryption role. Also create a separate CMK for control-plane audit log encryption so audit integrity is clear. :lock:

Chris L: A couple practical notes: we MUST never write plaintext DEKs to disk. Envelope flow we use today is: GenerateDataKey (CMK) -> keep plaintext DEK in memory -> use DEK to encrypt payload -> store ciphertext-DEK alongside encrypted object. For runtime perf we currently cache decrypted DEKs in memory for 300s (5m) for hosted API. For Private deployments behind VPCs I recommend a shorter default (60–120s) and make it configurable per-install. That reduces blast radius if a control-plane instance is compromised. Also ensure DEK cache uses secure in-memory structures and is wiped on GC.

Alex P: Good point on TTL. One rotation nuance: AWS KMS key rotation (automatic yearly rotation of key material) does NOT invalidate previously generated ciphertexts for the same CMK key-id — KMS keeps previous material available to decrypt. But if customer replaces the CMK (creates a new key and points policy to it), existing ciphertexts encrypted under the old key won't decrypt; we need a rewrap job for that case. Rewrap approach: for each stored ciphertext-DEK, call Decrypt with old CMK, then GenerateDataKey with new CMK and re-encrypt DEK, atomically swap in storage. Plan for paused traffic or dual-read fallback during rewrap.

Maya R: Also be careful with grants vs assume-role. For high QPS decrypts, CreateGrant (grants) is significantly cheaper than repeated policy checks; create a long-lived grant tied to the control-plane role. But grants complicate rotation: if we rotate to a different CMK, you must close out grants. Include grant cleanup in the playbook. Watch GrantToken semantics when you do concurrent create/grant operations.

sec-bot: Created SEC-4621: KMS BYOK + rewrap/rotation playbook (https://redwood.company/sec/SEC-4621) :white_check_mark:

Chris L: Example minimal key policy + trust snippet we should use as a baseline (customer CMK allowing cross-account access from the Redwood control plane role):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Id": "key-policy-example",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRootAccountUse",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodControlPlane",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/RedwoodControlPlaneRole"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:CreateGrant","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Chris L: And example CreateGrant pattern for high-throughput decrypts: `aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/customer-cmk --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/RedwoodControlPlaneRole --operations Decrypt --name "redwood-decrypt-grant"` — store the GrantId so we can retire it during rotation.

SRE Oncall: A few infra items — ensure the customer's networking allows KMS calls (kms.amazonaws.com) and CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey is enabled in their account so they have audit records. Recommend configuring a KMS VPC endpoint (interface endpoint) and restrict endpoint policy to only the control-plane ENIs + CloudTrail logging. Also check that endpoint policy prevents other principals in the account from abusing the CMK.

Alex P: TL;DR action items: (1) Maya draft key policy templates + BYOK checklist (including CloudTrail requirements), (2) Chris add DEK rewrap job + DEK cache TTL configurable (default 60s for Private), (3) SRE verify VPC endpoint policy + document network requirements, (4) Sec ops to add rotation playbook SEC-4621 with grant cleanup steps.

Maya R: I'll put the key policy templates in the SEC ticket and include a sample CloudTrail check script + required IAM ARNs.

Chris L: I'll prototype the rewrap tool as a idempotent job (can run multi-worker with leases) and add a migration mode with dual-read: try new CMK decrypt first, fallback to old CMK, then rewrap when successful.

SRE Oncall: I'll add an endpoint policy checklist to infra runbooks and verify we can create interface endpoints in the customer's account during onboarding.

Alex P: Let's meet quick tomorrow 10:00am PST to sign off on wording and timelines. Thanks everyone. :v:
